I organize partnership meetings every week, and I always start with the agenda. I write it three days before the meeting, and I circulate it the same day. First, I write the objective in one sentence. What do we want at the end of this call? Then I choose three agenda items, sometimes four, never more. Each item has a time slot and a name. For example, fifteen minutes, Daniel presents the new program. At the start of the meeting, I ask one person to take the minutes. And if something important comes up during the call, I say: good point, we are going to put it on the next agenda.

Last year I had a meeting with a partner from Mexico, and we had no agenda. We started with a small subject, the date of an event, and we talked about it for about forty minutes. Everybody had an opinion. Then somebody looked at the clock, and we had only five minutes left. The important subject, the budget, never happened. We had to reschedule, and the partner was not happy. Now I have a simple rule. I am going to send an agenda before every meeting, with a time slot for each item. And if a discussion takes too long, I will stop it and prioritize.
